mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to increase borrowing and investment, thereby boosting equity valuations and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, positively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following UNRATE falling below 7%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate indicates a robust labor market, which may lead to higher economic output and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following positive payroll employment and decreasing unemployment, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPI) may lead to inflation concerns, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which could negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a CPI increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates a strong housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an increase in housing starts, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong manufacturing sector, which may lead to increased economic output and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following an increase in industrial production, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales combined with GDP growth indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which may lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following increases in retail sales and GDP, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate may indicate a tightening monetary policy, which could lead to decreased borrowing and investment, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following a high FEDFUNDS rate, the hypothesis is rejected.
